disposition_mapping.rationale: Submission stays employee-initiated and unchanged in substance: the employee still originates the claim and still attaches receipts above the threshold (EXR-R-01, EXR-R-10). The only change is operational tolerance for asynchronous/offline submission; no decision authority moves.

Mechanical extraction is automated, but the council converged (hitl_designer's concession, finance_domain's concession, emerging_economy's objection) that it must remain a separately loggable function with its own confidence-threshold exception lane staffed by an AP analyst, not folded invisibly into submission or merged indistinguishably with policy-checking. This preserves traceability of which extraction confidence fed which downstream decision.

Deterministic rule-matching is automated and the mechanical majority passes straight through, but the step survives as a distinct, timestamped, inspectable artifact (EXR-R-07) with a human exception lane that can actually reject, hold, or adjust flagged lines, not merely view them. It is structurally sequenced to precede line manager approval (EXR-R-02), satisfied by construction since T-04 consumes T-03's output.

The council majority (pragmatist, finance_domain, emerging_economy, hitl_designer, accounting_standards, agentic_architect) held against maximalist's exception-only auto-approval design: a rules engine certifies policy compliance, not business legitimacy, and only a human manager can judge the latter, so every claim must still generate an explicit, logged attestation (EXR-R-08). What changes is the information content presented (structured flag summary) and channel resilience, which streamlines but does not remove the gate, and preserves actor separation from EXR-01 (EXR-R-03).

Finance review is explicitly unconstrained by design and is narrowed from 100% coverage to risk-triggered claims plus periodic sampling of the clean population, capturing most of the efficiency gain. It is kept as a function distinct from T-04 rather than merged into a single adjudication event, because the council majority held that business-legitimacy judgment and coding/evidence-sufficiency judgment are different competencies whose collapse would destroy post-hoc attributability (KB-02).

Posting is automated for mechanically resolvable lines but continues to consume the expense transaction date (EXR-R-04) and transaction-date exchange rate (EXR-R-05) as mandatory inputs, per KB-01/KB-07. Per the council's resolved conflict on FX sourcing, batch-cadence rate tables are accepted as compliant provided staleness is documented and consistently applied (KB-06); cutoff discipline (KB-03) is preserved via a mandatory GL-accountant checkpoint for period-straddling claims before close, and recognition is logged as a distinct event per KB-11.

Reimbursement survives (EXR-R-09) and still occurs only after a valid manager-approval event, now enforced as a hard programmatic precondition rather than a soft sequence (EXR-R-06). Automation of payment execution is accepted, but bank-detail-change verification is added as a non-bypassable control given its fraud profile, and the channel is made multi-rail (bank transfer, mobile money, cash) rather than single-rail, reflecting the resolved infrastructure conflict. Derecognition is logged as a distinct, linked event per KB-11.

Notification carries no judgment or accounting-standards content and the council was unanimous that it should fire automatically as a by-product of payment confirmation rather than remain a standalone human-performed step. The one substantive addition, carried over from emerging_economy's position, is that the merged notification must use multiple channels (not email/app-only) for parity across connectivity tiers.

steps.description: The employee originates the claim, entering expense details and attaching receipt images for claim lines above the receipt threshold. Submission supports asynchronous, store-and-forward operation so claims can be queued on intermittent connectivity and synced later; no automated agent submits on the employee's behalf.
inputs: Receipts for claim lines above the receipt threshold
steps.name: Claim submission with embedded receipt capture

steps.description: An extraction agent performs OCR/data extraction on receipt images, producing a structured claim record with a per-field confidence score. Extractions above the confidence threshold auto-populate; low-confidence lines (illegible, non-Latin script, non-standard formats) route to an AP-analyst exception queue for manual correction rather than being silently accepted. Kept as a distinct, separately loggable function from policy compliance so the specific extraction confidence that drove a downstream decision remains inspectable.
steps.name: Automated receipt extraction with confidence-based exception queue

steps.actor: AP analyst (exception adjudication), policy compliance agent
steps.description: A deterministic rules engine checks structured claim lines against policy limits, categories and per diem rates and writes a timestamped pass/flag artifact citing the policy clause applied, kept independently auditable from the extraction step. The engine never silently clears or rejects a flagged line; flagged, ambiguous, or policy-table-stale lines route to an AP analyst with authority to request information, adjust, or reject before the claim proceeds. This gate must complete, and its artifact must exist, before the claim reaches line manager approval.
steps.name: Automated policy compliance engine with exception adjudication

steps.description: The claimant's line manager reviews every claim and gives an explicit, logged attestation before it proceeds, regardless of whether the automated policy engine cleared it. The manager sees a structured summary of what was auto-cleared versus flagged and why, enabling low-friction approval for clean claims and substantive adjudication for flagged ones, but this step is never bypassed by claim cleanliness because manager attestation certifies business legitimacy, a judgment the policy engine cannot make. Approval is reachable through a low-bandwidth/SMS-equivalent fallback for unflagged claims; any flagged claim forces the manager onto a richer channel able to render the full summary.
steps.name: Line manager approval (universal gate, structured flag summary)

steps.description: Finance review is narrowed from a blanket check on every approved claim to a risk-triggered gate on claims with policy exceptions, above a materiality threshold, in high-risk categories, cross-currency, or carrying overrides, plus a periodic sample of the clean population to catch systematic rules-engine error. This remains structurally and actorally distinct from line manager approval: the manager certifies business legitimacy, finance certifies coding accuracy and evidentiary sufficiency, and the two attestations are never recorded as a single undifferentiated event.
inputs: Flag and exception record from T-03
steps.name: Risk-based finance review

steps.actor: GL accountant (exceptions, cutoff review), posting agent
steps.description: A posting agent applies the chart-of-accounts mapping and posts mechanically resolvable lines automatically, consuming the expense transaction date and the transaction-date exchange rate as mandatory inputs; rates may be sourced from a batch-updated table rather than a continuous real-time feed, provided the staleness bound is documented and applied consistently period over period. The agent emits a distinct, timestamped liability-recognised event per claim. Claims straddling a period boundary, unmapped cost centres, missing or disputed FX rates, or other estimation-adjacent lines escalate to the GL accountant, who remains accountable for cutoff discipline and FX anomaly review before period close; every automated posting is reversible, not merely overwritable.
steps.name: Automated posting with GL accountant exception and cutoff handling

steps.actor: AP analyst (bank-detail verification, failed-payment exceptions), payment agent
steps.description: A payment agent assembles and executes the reimbursement, enforcing a hard, programmatic precondition that a valid manager-approval event exists for the specific claim before it enters a payment run. Any claim where the employee's payee bank details are new or recently changed is held for mandatory independent human verification before release, regardless of channel. The design supports multiple disbursement channels (bank transfer, mobile money, cash disbursement with reconciliation) behind the same approval gate rather than assuming a single rail. On successful payment the agent emits a distinct, timestamped liability-extinguished event linked to the posting's liability-recognised event, and triggers an automatic, multi-channel (not email/app-only) notification to the employee as a direct by-product of payment confirmation.
steps.name: Automated reimbursement payment with bank-detail verification and notification
